overall: The AG found the Taunton City Council violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing a citizen letter among a quorum of members over email, though the initial distribution of the letter by email was permitted.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that a citizen's October 2011 letter to the Council was discussed by councilors over email without her knowledge, outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The email exchanges between members of the Council violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the letter was discussed by email and the complainant was denied a public forum on it; the Council argued agenda placement was not Council business.
allegations.key_passage: While the decision whether to place the letter on the agenda may be within the discretion of the Mayor and the City Clerk, the Council still has jurisdiction over addressing the content of the letter and ultimately deciding how to respond.

allegations.summary: Council argued that emailing the letter itself to members, and the Mayor's initial distribution email, were permitted administrative communications.
allegations.key_passage: We agree with the Council that it may distribute a letter over email.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, as ordered by the Attorney General.
remedy_passage: As a result of this violation, we order the Council's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
